# Proverbs 23 — Disagreement Log
**Generated by:** SOPHIA | **Threshold:** <70% word overlap

---

## 23:3 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | Do-not-desire his-delicacies, for it [is] bread-of deceptions. |
| LOGOS | Do not desire his delicacies, for they are deceptive food. |
| PNEUMA | Don't be seduced by their fancy food — it's bait. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | Do-not-toil to-become-rich; from-your-[own]-understanding cease. |
| LOGOS | Do not toil to acquire wealth; be discerning enough to desist. |
| PNEUMA | Don't exhaust yourself trying to get rich. Have the sense to stop. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

| Translator | Rendering |

| EMET | Do-not-eat [the]-bread-of [one]-evil-of eye, and-do-not-desire his-delicacies, |
| LOGOS | Do not eat the bread of a man who is stingy; do not desire his delicacies, |
| PNEUMA | Don't eat with a stingy person, and don't be tempted by their fancy food, |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 23:7 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | For as he-reckons in-his-soul, so he [is]. 'Eat and-drink,' he-says to-you, but-his-heart [is]-not with-you. |
| LOGOS | For he is like one who is inwardly calculating. 'Eat and drink!' he says to you, but his heart is not with you. |
| PNEUMA | Because they're calculating every bite you take. They say, 'Help yourself!' but they resent every morsel. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

| LOGOS | You will vomit up the morsels that you have eaten, and waste your pleasant words. |
| PNEUMA | You'll end up sick to your stomach, and all your kind words will have been wasted. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.
